title: Sprint-window crediting and on-call handover protocol for launch trains
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Define and operationalize a consistent sprint-window crediting mechanism and an on-call handover protocol tailored to cross-surface release trains (runtime / console / API). Goal is to remove ambiguity about ownership, ensure teams receive sprint credit for launch work, and reduce toil and incidents during cutover windows.

Problem statement: In the last three release trains we observed duplicated effort, missed handovers between squads, and unclear sprint crediting for out-of-cycle bugfights during launch weeks. This results in morale issues, uneven sprint velocity accounting, and occasionally delayed rollbacks. We need a lightweight but enforceable protocol that ties into the launch calendar and on-call rotations.

Scope:
- Define sprint-window crediting rules (how to attribute launch-related work and overtime to the launching sprint vs maintenance sprint).
- Create a standardized on-call handover checklist for pre-launch, cutover, and post-launch stabilization windows.
- Add a 'launch-credit' tag/label convention in Linear and GitHub issues and define minimal required metadata.
- Produce a short runbook section for SRE/On-call escalation during launch windows.
- Integrate a calendar-based crediting signal into the launch planner (Console) so PMs and Eng leads can see anticipated credits.
- Pilot the protocol during the runtime-1.20 train with two squads across runtime and console.

Out of scope: compensation policy changes, HR time-off accounting, or long-term payroll processes. This ticket focuses on crediting/attribution in planning and operational handover.

Acceptance criteria:
1) A one-page operational spec published in Confluence with: crediting rules, tagging convention, handover checklist, and responsibilities matrix.
2) Linear label "launch-credit:2026-04" defined and applied in pilot work items; at least 12 pilot issues tagged.
3) On-call handover checklist added to the on-call runbook and validated by SRE and two Eng managers.
4) Pilot report (one-page) showing before/after metrics for handover success (on-call escalations reduced, mean time to acknowledge during cutover improved).
5) Launch planner integration prototype (calendar overlay) that surfaces planned credit windows for squads in Console.

Deliverables:
- Confluence doc: "Sprint crediting & handover for launch trains" (link in attachments).
- Runbook addition: "Launch window on-call checklist".
- Linear and GitHub tagging guidance (short doc snippet).
- Pilot retro and metrics dashboard snapshot.

Stakeholders:
- PMs: Aisha Patel (Lead), Priya Nair (Console PM)
- Eng leads: Liam Carter (Runtime), Mei Huang (Console), Rafael Ortiz (API)
- SRE/On-call: SRE rotation leads (On-call team)
- Design/DevEx: (for Console calendar UI) — Marcus Lin

Success metrics:
- <= 1 missed handover per launch train in pilot (baseline was 3).
- MTTA during cutover windows improved by 20% against last train.
- 80% of pilot issues correctly tagged with launch-credit before code freeze.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Teams treat crediting as bureaucratic checkbox. Mitigation: keep rules simple; surface benefits in velocity reports.
- Risk: Calendar integration scope creep. Mitigation: prototype as read-only overlay for pilot; defer write-back to later cycle.

Rollout plan:
1) Week 1: Draft Confluence spec and tagging guide. Share with Eng leads and SRE for feedback.
2) Week 2: Finalize on-call checklist; implement Linear label and GitHub label repo guidance.
3) Week 3: Integrate read-only calendar overlay in Console staging for pilot squads and train.
4) Week 4: Run pilot during runtime-1.20 train; collect metrics and run retro.
5) Week 5: Iterate and publish final playbook; propose org-wide adoption for next quarter.

Notes on measurement: We'll use Console telemetry to collect cutover alerts and Linear query counts for tagged issues. The pilot report will include raw numbers and qualitative feedback from engineers and on-call.
